text: You enter the bank, hoping for a quick transaction. You might even look for a familiar face, expecting a personal connection to make things smoother.
But next time, it’s someone new. And again after that, someone else. It truly feels like you never see the same teller twice in a row.
You start to wonder why. Is the bank just randomly assigning staff? Or is there some secret system preventing you from building any real rapport?
Banks are complex systems balancing fluctuating demand. Tellers have different skills, shifts, and tasks beyond just the service counter.
So instead of one slow queue for *your* specific teller, staff are distributed across all available stations, ensuring someone is always ready.
Now, approaching the counter, you don't just see random rotation. You see an optimized flow, designed to keep the entire operation moving efficiently.
